paragraphs.text: An ISACA chapter is created when like-minded individuals see an opportunity to formalize and expand the benefits of being in a local community, which includes connecting with others who share interests, getting involved through volunteerism, welcoming others, and raising awareness of ISACA’s mission and purpose.
ISACA chapters advance those goals and sustain a localized organization that benefits the community and the broader profession, tailored to their context.

Chapters that have adopted and sustained mature practices see better outcomes regarding member satisfaction, retention of members, growth of certification holders, and influence through advocacy efforts. However, attaining excellence takes time; it requires systematic planning and strategy development.

Chapter 360 is a resource for volunteer chapter leaders that simplifies the role of sustaining the organization and equips them with tools to maximize the chapter's potential. It guides volunteer leaders to consistently deliver (to their utmost abilities) ISACA's offerings throughout its area, based on local needs and using preferred practices.
Chapter 360 was inspired by the format of CMMI V 3.0® and COBIT®, which provide practices that can be tailored to achieve success for the chapter from every angle.

As a chapter follows this model, it will provide a 360 view of the chapter, uncover any unknown opportunities, gaps, or risks, and help the chapter achieve relevance, value, scalability, and trustworthiness.

For chapters seeking growth, developing strategies in focus areas most relevant to a chapter can increase its potential, expand its capabilities, ensure scalability, amplify its local strategy, and accelerate performance for its established goals.
Through the Chapter 360 self-assessment tool, ISACA Global can ensure volunteer chapter leaders have the most important and relevant resources based on their chapter’s unique needs and challenges.
The Chapter 360 tool comprises six key Focus Areas, and within each Focus Area, there are three to six Practice Areas. For example:
The full view of Focus and Practice Areas is as follows:

As part of the self-assessment scoring, the Focus Area “Manage Chapter Operations” is foundational to the Focus Areas “Deliver Local Member Experience” and “Facilitate Professional Development Locally.”
When you complete a self-assessment, the scores for “Deliver Local Member Experience” and “Facilitate Professional Development Locally” also will include your ratings for “Manage Chapter Operations.”

ISACA Global will provide a link for self-assessment annually so that we can gather results and determine how to prioritize the development of resources, templates, and tools for our chapters. Upon completion of the annual assessment, your chapter’s aggregated results will be available in the document library for your chapter on Engage. As we continue the development of the Chapter 360 tool, we aim to have this integrated into the Chapter Leader Portal. Until then, you can submit your self-assessment at https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/TXN57LW

Once you’ve completed an assessment for your chapter, you will receive a report with the scores provided for each practice area and rolled up into the overall focus area. If one or more leaders from your chapter have taken the survey independently, the scores will be averaged into one final score. The scoring method is straightforward and simple:
Each practice area is assessed on a scale of 1 to 5. (Visual below)

Focus area scores are an average of the practice area scores it includes. Please note: the scores for Deliver Local Member Experience and Facilitate Professional Development Locally will also include your ratings for Manage Chapter Operations.
Your chapter’s overall score is an average of all practice area scores.

Operational excellence involves carefully planning, executing, and assessing a chapter’s services and experiences. This Focus Area is foundational to Managing Local Member Experience and Dispensing Knowledge Locally.
Long-Term Success: A chapter’s operations are key to its stability, growth, and success.
Empowered Leaders: Achieving operational excellence helps leaders share knowledge better, recognize members, and make a local impact.
Community Building: Members will have rich experiences, which will increase their engagement and loyalty, helping them reach their professional goals.

What it is: Leading an ISACA chapter involves organizing services and programs with the help of volunteers. The goal is to support ISACA members in growing their careers. By defining this portfolio, chapter leaders can bring value to their members and community.
Each chapter’s portfolio can be different. Some meet ISACA’s basic standards, while others also invest in becoming or staying in an accredited training program (ATP or ATO).
Rewarding Experiences: When services match member needs and are delivered quickly and effectively, members are more likely to be satisfied and succeed in reaching their professional goals.
Efficient Processes: Identifying and removing unnecessary services helps chapters run more efficiently and save money.
Smart Decision-Making: A clear understanding of chapter services and programs enables leaders to make smarter choices about resource use, leading to better overall outcomes.
1.1 Evaluate & Share Member Needs: Gather, record, and analyze data on what members need from services and programs. Then share this information with relevant stakeholders.
Benefit: Discover which services and programs most improve member satisfaction.
Report: Chapter-Specific Member Needs Survey Results
Template: Satisfaction Surveys, Various (Event, Virtual Event, Conference, Virtual Conference, Chapter Satisfaction, etc.)
1.2 Plan a Service & Program Strategy: Develop a plan that offers new or improved services and programs that align with strategic goals and available resources.
Benefit: Find services that best meet member needs.
1.3 Identify Services & Programs: Develop a list of current services and programs with up-to-date descriptions.
Benefit: Ensure member needs are met and that experiences are consistent.
1.4 Define Standard Operating Procedures [SOPs]: Develop, keep updated, and use the set of updated Standard Operating Procedures [SOPs].
Benefit: Speed up implementation processes and consistency throughout new and updated services.
What it is: Managing financial activities and prioritizing spending with budgeting measures ensures fair allocation of funds within the chapter.

Financial Confidence: Chapters have successful financial stability, resource allocation, financial performance, informed decision-making, performance evaluation, stakeholder confidence, and risk mitigation.
Operational Ease: Chapters stay within their budget, maximize financial performance, and make informed decisions to meet strategic goals, balancing both revenue and costs.
2.1 Create High-Level Estimates: Work with stakeholders to review chapter needs / assumptions, helping create up-to-date, high-level estimates to carry out chapter operations.
Benefit: Prevent budget overruns through efficient tracking and timely corrective actions to ensure on-time, budget-aligned delivery.
2.2 Maintain Scope: Collaborate with stakeholders to define scope, gather data for estimates, and identify scope constraints.
Benefit: Meet objectives and avoid rework.
2.3 Establish a Budget: Based on size estimates, develop and record a chapter budget. Collect and use historical data to develop, calibrate, or recalibrate the chapter budget.
Benefit: Solidify the budget and boost chapter performance.
What it is: Security management protects chapter assets. It keeps people, data, systems, ideas, and physical items safe by stopping unauthorized access, use, sharing, changes, or damage.
Asset Protection: Helps prevent financial loss, harm to the chapter’s reputation, injuries, property damage, and other bad outcomes.
Reduced Risk: Reduces risks of security incidents, such as data breaches, cyberattacks, or other intrusions that can impact a chapter's bottom line and operational effectiveness.
Adherence Ease: Ensures compliance with applicable local and global regulations to avoid penalties.
Privacy Protection: In today's digital world, individuals entrust organizations with their data. Security management can help chapters protect this data and keep their members' trust.
3.1 Create Security & Privacy Policies: Develop and update a policy to guide on security and privacy matters.
Benefit: Meet privacy and security needs.
3.2 Identify Needs & Issues: Identify and record security needs and issues.
Benefit: Reduce disruptions from security and privacy issues affecting the chapter’s efforts.
List: Sample Security & Privacy Needs, Issues
3.3 Prioritize Needs & Issues: Review, prioritize, and update security and privacy issues that occur within the chapter, while tracking actions taken to resolve them.
Benefit: Address security and privacy needs.
ISACA SOP: Security & Privacy Action Plan
3.4 Address Needs & Issues: Develop and maintain an approach for identifying, handling, and monitoring privacy and security needs/issues.
Benefit: Prioritize and address security and privacy issues in a consistent manner.
List: Risk-Based Approaches for Handing Security and Privacy Threats
What it is: Managing ISACA chapter operations involves planning and prioritizing resources to meet goals. This helps ensure consistent delivery of services that satisfy members and community needs.
Effective Planning: Reduce costs and improve productivity.
Experience Satisfaction: Contribute to overall member satisfaction, engagement, and loyalty.

Growing Community (or Chapter Visibility): Satisfied members are more likely to renew their membership and certifications, recruit new members, and provide word-of-mouth testimonials to their colleagues.
Competitive Edge: Providing high-quality services positively contributes to the chapter’s and ISACA’s brand and competitive advantage.
Weblink: Site Admin Community (Site Admin Only)
4.2 Develop Tasks: Create a task list, review it with stakeholders, and revise as needed.
Benefit: Identify and address chapter requirements.
4.3 Assign Tasks: Promote and assign volunteer roles and responsibilities.

4.4 Establish Preferred Practices: Develop and update preferred practices for accomplishing tasks while considering chapter objectives, approach, requirements, and resources. Revise practices as necessary.
Benefit: Keep stakeholders focused on accomplishing their specific objectives.
4.5 Equip Volunteers with Knowledge & Skills: Identify and plan to provide the knowledge and skills needed for volunteers to accomplish tasks. Fill in the gap where necessary.
Benefit: Efficient and effective use of volunteer resources.
What it is: Vendor management is key for controlling costs, reducing risks, monitoring performance, building relationships, encouraging innovation, ensuring compliance, and staying adaptable.
Reliable Partnerships: Ensures the chapter has reliable, high-quality vendors/suppliers, minimizes risks, and optimizes costs.
Aligned Efforts: Ensures chapter-vendor alignment towards shared objectives.
5.1 Establish a Vendor Management Policy: Define, document, and update a policy for vendor management.
Benefit: Maintain consistency across vendor agreements.
RACI Chart: Sample Vendor Management RACI
5.2 Choose a Vendor: Establish a way to find potential vendors, request proposals, and evaluate them throughout the selection process.
Benefit: Select vendors that fit the project’s needs.
5.3 Align on Contracts: Create and finalize vendor agreements by negotiating terms, reaching agreements, and reviewing contracts.
Benefit: Meet scope and price expectations.
5.4 Align on Deliverables: Accept vendor deliverables based on contractual requirements.
Benefit: Obtain the agreed-on vendor deliverable(s).
5.5 Process Invoices: Process vendor invoices in accordance with agreements.
Benefit: Maintain good working relationships with vendors.
5.6 Maintain Vendor Relationships: Identify key people and their needs, document their impact on the agreement, and share with affected stakeholders.
Benefit: Reduce vendor disruptions while fulfilling agreements.
5.7 Maintain a Vendor Database: Set vendor data goals and maintain a data management strategy to meet them.
Benefit: Keep accurate, up-to-date vendor data.
5.8 Leverage Strategic Partnerships: Keep an updated and detailed list of services with current partnerships. Leverage relationships where possible.
Benefit: Align needs with partnership resources.
5.9 Assess Vendor Performance: Track performance metrics and address any issues when necessary.
Benefit: Improve performance management and increase likelihood of meeting vendor goals.
Delivering the local member experience involves creating a welcoming community, connecting members, and recognizing achievements.
Thriving Community: Fostering a culture of inclusiveness and transparency strengthens community, boosts engagement, and enhances retention.
Increased Participation: Engaging members and encouraging them to volunteer boosts engagement and retention.

Culture of Gratitude: Recognizing member achievements increases engagement and retention. Achievements should be accurate, timely, relevant, personalized, region-specific, and mindful of circumstances.

Credibility Growth: Acknowledgment highlights the value of membership and certification for prospects and members. Regularly recognize personal and professional achievements, like certifications, promotions, and membership tenure.

What it is: Culture management fosters a productive and positive environment where everyone can contribute and thrive. It involves aligning with ISACA’s values and building a chapter culture that supports them.
Community Building: Members satisfied with the chapter culture are likely to be engaged, productive, and loyal. They are also more likely to be willing to go above and beyond for their chapter.
Innovation Hub: When members feel safe to take risks and share ideas, they are more likely to offer innovative solutions.
Retention & Growth: Members are less likely to leave a chapter if they’re happy with its culture, boosting retention and satisfaction.
Performance Boost: A positive culture improves financial performance by attracting members and sponsors, enhancing experiences, and fostering innovation.
Increased Trust & Transparency: A key to a positive culture is enabling transparency between stakeholders, which builds trust, respect, and appreciation.
Chapter Alignment: Improved communication ensures that everyone involved clearly understands the goals, project, or program.
1.1 Leverage Chapter 360: Use Chapter 360 tools and resources to plan, manage, and lead.
Benefit: Reduce management effort and cost. Increase satisfaction, efficiency, and effectiveness.
1.2 Focus on the Fundamentals: Perform the fundamental, core competencies of a chapter.
Benefit: Oversee a chapter that has a solid foundation.
1.3 Leverage Trainings: Identify and provide resources to boost performance and expand on fundamental and core competencies of the chapter.
Benefit: Improve process efforts by having sufficient resources.
1.4 Champion ISACA’s Mission, Vision, Purpose: Evaluate and share ISACA's mission, vision, and purpose, locally.
Benefit: Increase chapter relevance and link global mission to local context.
Reference ISACA Strategic Competencies: Lead with ISACA's strategic competencies in mind.
Benefit: Increase chapter leader impact and connect strategic competencies to local context.
1.6 Demonstrate ISACA Values: Exemplify and champion ISACA's values.
Benefit: Boost credibility and align global values with local context.
1.8 Promote the ISACA Foundation: Expand ISACA Foundation’s local reach by removing any barriers.
Benefit: Grow the community and welcome upcoming generations.
1.9 Promote SheLeadsTech: Expand access by removing or eliminating barriers with She Leads Tech locally.
Benefit: Expand the community and welcome the next generation.

What it is: Managing community events involves planning and organizing gatherings where people connect and share a common cause.
Increased Impact: A well-managed community or networking event will succeed in attendance, engagement, and outcomes.

Meaningful Network: By facilitating interactions with people who share interests and a profession, attendees can learn about others' experiences, find potential mentors and collaborators, and expand their networks.
Center for Opportunities: Community and networking events can lead to discovering job openings, internships, grants, and other opportunities.
Relationship Facilitation: By helping attendees connect, you can foster relationships beneficial for the chapter and participants’ careers and personal lives.
2.1 Establish an Event Strategy: Create, update, and implement an event strategy that includes program delivery, volunteers, communications, systems, and budget.
List: Event Strategy Components (e.g., ISACA Global membership and renewal calendars, ISACA Global event calendars, etc.)
2.2 Choose an Event Environment: Select and set up the best event environment, whether virtual or in-person, while keeping members and stakeholders informed.
Benefit: Meet participant needs and event objectives.

2.4 Define Event Standard Operating Procedures [SOPs]: Create and follow procedures and best practices for event production, program delivery, operations, volunteers, and communications.
Benefit: Curate an event that meets participant needs.

2.5 Coordinate Event Delivery: Ensure each event component follows the SOP (Standard of Practice) and verify that requirements are met (e.g., program delivery, volunteers, communications, systems, budget).
Benefit: Reduce total event cost, production time, and rework.
2.6 Deliver the Event: Assemble the event components and deliver a seamless experience to participants.

What it is: Managing member communications involves planning, organizing, and directing information flow through meetings, newsletters, email, and social media.
Trust and Rapport: When members feel they are being kept informed, they are more likely to be engaged and supportive of the chapter.
Community Belonging: Effective communication fosters belonging and shared purpose, boosting morale and positive culture.
Diversity and Inclusion: By listening to and respecting different perspectives, leaders can help create a more inclusive environment for everyone (see Chapter Culture practice area).
3.1 Identify Pertinent Laws & Regulations: Identify and document laws and regulations relevant to community communications.
Benefit: Reduce risk by following local laws and regulations.
List: Known Laws & Regulations (e.g., GDPR), including Pertinent Aspects
3.2 Identify Channels, Tools & Assets: Identify and document available channels, tools, and assets for the chapter's communication strategy, and determine community preferences.
Benefit: Align communication strategy with available resources for seamless communication avenues.
Website Link: Link to Engage Microsite
List: Communication Channels, including Channel Guidance

3.3 Establish a Communications Strategy: Develop a member communication strategy with clear and prioritized objectives. Choose channels, tools, and assets that help meet these objectives, define necessary activities, and assign roles and responsibilities.
Benefit: Provide structure and direction for member communications. Maximize impact while minimizing cost and effort.
Website Link: Member Needs Survey Results
3.4 Use Communications System: Identify and acquire communications systems that meet requirements and ensure that they are easy to use.
Benefit: Minimize costs, effort, and time needed to perform the work.
3.5 Adhere to Brand Standards & Assets: Reference the ISACA brand style guide to access brand assets and standard guidelines.
Benefit: Deliver high-quality communications that are on-brand, using brand-approved assets.
3.6 Implement the Strategy: Create and follow a communications plan using strategy and past data. Regularly update the plan, identify improvements, and review it with stakeholders.
Benefit: Reduce the time and effort needed to plan and coordinate.
3.7 Measure Performance: Evaluate communication systems using a clear criterion. Update criteria regularly and identify best practices for future use.
Benefit: Establish benchmarks and best practices.
Task Checklist: Measuring Performance Preferred Practices
3.8 Improve Performance: Identify and record opportunities for future improvement.
Benefit: Meet communications goals and objectives.
What it is: Volunteers are vital, offering diverse skills and perspectives. Utilizing their dedication and skills helps achieve chapter goals, strengthen community, and drive success.
Mission Fulfillment: Volunteers play a vital role in helping chapters achieve their mission and build capacity by offering their time, skills, and expertise.
Deeper Connections: Engaging members as volunteers strengthens their connection to the chapter and improves their experience.
Leadership Development: Chapters can nurture future leaders and ensure succession by identifying top volunteers, assessing their potential, and offering development opportunities.
Skill Growth: Volunteer opportunities allow individuals to learn or practice skills they may not use in their daily jobs, creating more well-rounded leaders.
Network Expansion: Volunteer connections bring new partners, diverse ideas, and an expanded network to support the chapter’s goals.
Lasting Impact: Volunteer connections foster loyalty among ISACA members, their chapter, and community with an added desire to leave a lasting impact.
4.1 Set an Organization Structure: Create a volunteer structure that defines authority delegation.
Benefit: Provide volunteers with authority and accountability to achieve outcomes effectively.
Presentation: Board and Committee Level Structure Visualization
4.2 Establish Volunteer Role Descriptions: Define volunteer role descriptions and specify their required tasks and skills.
Benefit: Align volunteer efforts to desired chapter outcomes.
Task Checklists: Various Sample Task Checklists
Template: She Leads Tech Role Description
4.3 Delegate Volunteer Opportunities: Once selected for a role, communicate volunteer roles and responsibilities in accordance with chapter bylaws and provide support.
Benefit: Achieve assigned roles and responsibilities.
Template: Benefits of Volunteering as a Chapter Leader
Template: Social Media and Email Templates
4.5 Leverage System Preferences: Develop and use communication and coordination systems.
Benefit: Increase productivity through effective information sharing.

4.6 Define Leadership Pathways: Use organizational charts and volunteer taxonomies to clarify chapter capabilities and leadership paths. Identify essential volunteer roles, assess capacity, and plan to increase where needed.
Benefit: Maximize consistent performance of the chapter.
4.7 Manage Transitions: Manage the transition of volunteers in and out of roles, receiving feedback from exit interviews or surveys to identify potential areas for improvement.
Benefit: Fulfill volunteer roles and responsibilities productively through transition seasons.
4.8 Celebrate Volunteer Impact: Develop and implement strategies and methods for recognizing volunteers.
Template: End of Volunteer Term Thank You
What it is: Managing local member and volunteer recognition involves acknowledging and appreciating contributions and loyalty, ranging from verbal praise to formal award programs.
Participation Motivators: Foster a culture of appreciation through recognition because publicly acknowledging members can be a powerful motivator.
Consistent Celebrations: Provide recognition opportunities that are consistent and equitable year over year. Examples may include years of service, volunteer hours, earning certifications, etc.
Growing Contributors: Invite honorees to contribute to training events, content creation, etc.
5.1 Establish a Recognition Policy: Develop a plan for recognizing members and volunteers using different recognition categories to establish consistency. Review with stakeholders for approval.
Benefit: Reduce member and volunteer churn.
5.2 Evaluate Contributions & Accomplishments: Evaluate contributions and achievements using policy standards. Update recognition criteria as needed and document any recognitions given.
Benefit: Deliver high-quality and standardized recognition.

5.3 Recognize Members & Volunteers: Show gratitude and appreciation to members through meaningful and intangible methods like a verbal "thank you", SMS text, quick phone call, e-mail, or handwritten note.
Benefit: Improve member and volunteer satisfaction.

5.4 Award Members & Volunteers: Depending on preference, privately thank and/or publicly recognize members and volunteers for their contributions and accomplishments. Reference local and regional guidelines for gift giving (e.g. a plaque, certificate, or item to display.) and ceremonies or galas (Annual General Meeting: AGM).
Benefit: Promote future member and volunteer engagement and contributions and avoid volunteer churn.

What it is: Managing requests involves promptly and transparently addressing comments, questions, and feedback. Managing incidents is handling situations that disrupt or impact the member experience and chapter operations.
Improved Satisfaction: Providing a quick and efficient response to requests and incidents can improve member satisfaction.
Reduced Costs: Preventing and resolving incidents quickly can reduce the costs associated with dissatisfied members and attrition.
Improved Compliance: A well-defined process for handling requests and incidents demonstrates that the chapter is taking steps to protect its assets and members.
Reduced Risk: Proactively managing requests and incidents can reduce the risk of disruptions to the member experience and protect the chapter’s reputation and bottom line.

Built trust: When members feel heard and understand the situation, they trust their leaders are doing the best for the greater good and that there is consistency and fairness in the process, even if their request is denied.
6.1 Establish a Request & Incident Policy: Record and resolve all requests and incidents, keeping track of their status.
Benefit: Manage unexpected situations while fulfilling commitments.

6.2 Response Plan: Develop, update, and follow a response approach for requests and incidents. Identify typical types, record useful information for management and prevention, define incident criteria, update workarounds, and document lessons learned.
Benefit: Maintain member satisfaction by consistently and efficiently addressing requests and incidents.
List: Request & Incident Types, Sample Resolutions
6.3 Resolve Requests & Incidents: Monitor and resolve each request and incident, escalating as needed until closure.
Benefit: Maximize the effectiveness of request and incident resolution to reduce disruption.

Governance protocols equip the chapter's board of directors to meet the needs of members, volunteers, and employees (if applicable).
Prioritization Setting: Effective chapter governance prioritizes adding value, mitigating risk, and appropriately fostering innovation.
Regulation Compliance: Transparency into governance practices ensures the chapter maintains credibility and compliance (legal and regulatory).
Decision Alignment: Decisions align clearly with chapter strategies, objectives, and bylaws.
Implementation Success: Governance structures and processes are implemented, supported, monitored, and routinely assessed.
Local Integration: Industry standards, guidance, regulations, local laws, and best practices are tailored to your chapter's specific locale.
What it is: Strategy management involves developing, implementing, and monitoring to ensure alignment with ISACA Global's goals, optimal resource use, and the achievement of established goals.
Competitive Edge: A clear and well-defined strategy will help chapters achieve their goals and surpass competitors.
Resource Optimization: Chapters focus investments on critical success areas, preventing resource wastage on unlikely initiatives.
Decision Alignment: Decisions are aligned with chapter’s goals and objectives.
Motivation Boost: Members have a clear understanding of the chapter's goals and objectives, offering insights into how they can contribute to its success through volunteer opportunities.
United Vision: Members have a shared vision and values to rally around.

What it is: Governance management involves overseeing and directing a chapter's activities in alignment with its values, goals, and objectives. It includes establishing comprehensive policies and procedures, monitoring performance, and implementing corrective actions as needed. This management is crucial for ensuring that a chapter is well-managed and that resources are utilized effectively.

Decision Alignment: A decision-making framework to ensure that choices align with the best interests of the chapter and its members. Streamlined Experiences: Resources are used effectively, and processes are streamlined.
Reduced Risk: Checks and balances to help identify and mitigate potential risks, protecting the chapter from financial loss, reputational damage, and other negative consequences.

Growing Reputation: Chapters demonstrate that they are well-managed and committed to good governance practices - factors that can help attract members and partners in academia, government, and enterprise.

Benefit: Improve processes to meet chapter objectives.

2.2 Comply to Bylaws: Chapter board members review the compliance checklist, assign tasks, and ensure submission aligns with bylaws.
Benefit: Improve processes to meet chapter objectives.

why.title: Participation Motivators
why.text: Foster a culture of appreciation through recognition because publicly acknowledging members can be a powerful motivator.

why.title: Consistent Celebrations
why.text: Provide recognition opportunities that are consistent and equitable year over year. Examples may include years of service, volunteer hours, earning certifications, etc.

why.title: Growing Contributors

practices.text: Develop a plan for recognizing members and volunteers using different recognition categories to establish consistency. Review with stakeholders for approval.

practiceAreas.name: Requests & Incidents
practiceAreas.whatItIs: Managing requests involves promptly and transparently addressing comments, questions, and feedback. Managing incidents is handling situations that disrupt or impact the member experience and chapter operations.

why.title: Improved Satisfaction
why.text: Providing a quick and efficient response to requests and incidents can improve member satisfaction.

why.title: Reduced Costs
why.text: Preventing and resolving incidents quickly can reduce the costs associated with dissatisfied members and attrition.

why.title: Improved Compliance
why.text: A well-defined process for handling requests and incidents demonstrates that the chapter is taking steps to protect its assets and members.

why.title: Reduced Risk
why.text: Proactively managing requests and incidents can reduce the risk of disruptions to the member experience and protect the chapter’s reputation and bottom line.

why.title: Built trust
why.text: When members feel heard and understand the situation, they trust their leaders are doing the best for the greater good and that there is consistency and fairness in the process, even if their request is denied.

practices.text: Record and resolve all requests and incidents, keeping track of their status.
practices.benefit: Manage unexpected situations while fulfilling commitments.

practices.text: Develop, update, and follow a response approach for requests and incidents. Identify typical types, record useful information for management and prevention, define incident criteria, update workarounds, and document lessons learned.
practices.benefit: Maintain member satisfaction by consistently and efficiently addressing requests and incidents.

practices.title: Resolve Requests & Incidents
practices.text: Monitor and resolve each request and incident, escalating as needed until closure.
practices.benefit: Maximize the effectiveness of request and incident resolution to reduce disruption.

practiceAreas.name: Risk Management
practiceAreas.whatItIs: Risk management involves proactively identifying and addressing potential losses or injuries. It's essential for chapter operations, protecting against financial losses, reputational harm, and other negative outcomes.

why.title: Reduced Risk
why.text: Minimizes the likelihood of adverse events occurring.

why.title: Chapter Protection
why.text: Protecting both physical assets, such as buildings and equipment, and intangible assets, like intellectual property and member data.

why.title: Decision-Making Ease
why.text: Understanding the chapter's risks facilitates better decision-making, which can help achieve the chapter's goals.

why.title: Regulation Compliance
why.text: By managing risk effectively, chapters can ensure compliance and avoid costly fines and penalties.

why.title: Improved Morale
why.text: When members see the chapter taking risks seriously, they gain confidence in its future, therefore increasing satisfaction and loyalty.

practices.benefit: Reduce risk impact and capitalize on opportunities to achieve objectives.

practices.text: Analyze and prioritize identified risks and opportunities. Assess impacts, probabilities, benefits, and costs. Rank based on priority, and develop a comprehensive analysis report.

practices.title: Monitor Risk & Opportunities
practices.text: Monitor and periodically review risks or opportunities, updating as new information arises.

why.title: Leader Empowerment
why.text: When individuals are empowered to lead, they are more likely to be engaged and productive.

why.title: Innovation Hub
why.text: When individuals are encouraged to share ideas, they are more likely to produce new and innovative solutions to problems.

why.title: Meaningful Contributions
why.text: When individuals feel part of something positive and more significant than themselves, they are more likely to be happy and motivated.

why.title: Giving Back Mindset
why.text: When people feel valued and have opportunities to lead and contribute, they are more likely to engage and volunteer for leadership roles in the chapter.

why.title: Seamless Transitions
why.text: A comprehensive chapter leader succession plan ensures seamless transitions and reduces disruptions to chapter operations.

practices.title: Plan Continuity
practices.text: Create and follow continuity plans to resume essential functions. Identify threats, validate plans with stakeholders, and ensure secure access to critical information. Protect data and revise plans as needed.

why.text: Non-compliance can lead to the loss of assets, such as money, data, and intellectual property. This can damage the chapter’s financial stability and ability to provide services to members and compete.

why.title: Reputation Stability
why.text: Non-compliance can damage the chapter's reputation and make it difficult to attract members or relationships in academia, government, or enterprise.

practiceAreas.name: Enterprise Relationships
practiceAreas.whatItIs: Managing enterprise relationships involves building and nurturing connections with key business stakeholders who influence training and credentialing decisions. This advocacy offers businesses access to ISACA's performance-based learning, top certifications, membership, and ongoing professional education. Some ISACA chapters have become Accredited Training Organizations (ATO), enabling them to train enterprises.

why.title: Established Credentials
why.text: Requiring credentialing by enterprises strengthens the profession and advances digital trust ambitions.

why.title: Economic Development
why.text: Promoting initiatives stimulating investment, innovation, and job creation within the industry leads to overall economic growth.

why.title: Workforce Development
why.text: Promoting training and development programs addresses business needs, enhances workforce mobility, and fosters collaboration between industry and ISACA.

why.title: Industry Promotion and Reputation
why.text: Promoting digital trust professions enhances their visibility and reputation.

practiceAreas.name: Community Communications
practiceAreas.whatItIs: Community communications involves planning and managing information to the non-member community, enhancing ISACA's image and awareness through sessions, media, email, and social media.

why.title: Industry Presence
why.text: Increasing awareness of ISACA can establish it and the chapter as industry leaders and trainers, while building relationships with media and industry partners.

why.title: Network Support
why.text: Strong relationships support chapter growth goals.

why.title: Credibility Establishment
why.text: Creating awareness of ISACA can help foster a sense of pride among members and credibility within the community.

why.title: Amplified Messaging
why.text: A chapter’s community communications are an opportunity to contextualize information and initiatives from ISACA Global and extend our collective reach.

practices.title: Establish Laws & Regulations
practices.text: Identify and document laws and regulations relevant to community communications.
practices.benefit: Reduce risk by communicating in a manner that adheres to local laws and regulations.

practices.title: Identify Channels, Tools & Resources
practices.text: Identify and document available channels, tools, and assets for the chapter's communication strategy, and determine community preferences.
practices.benefit: Ensure the scope of the communication strategy aligns with available resources.

practices.title: Establish a Communications Strategy
practices.text: Develop a member communication strategy with clear and prioritized objectives. Choose channels, tools, and assets that help meet these objectives, define necessary activities, and assign roles and responsibilities.
practices.benefit: Provide structure and direction for member communications that maximizes impact while minimizing cost and effort.

practices.title: Use a Communications Systems
practices.text: Identify and acquire communications systems that meet requirements and ensure that they are easy to use.
practices.benefit: Avoid waste by focusing resources only on the processes needed to do perform the work.

practices.title: Plan & Coordinate Communications
practices.text: Develop a communications plan based on strategy and past data. Identify areas for improvement and review the plan with stakeholders for necessary updates.
practices.benefit: Reduce the time and effort needed to coordinate and put the plan into action while focusing on what works.

practices.title: Apply Brand Standards & Brand Assets
practices.text: Reference the ISACA brand style guide to access brand assets and standard guidelines.
practices.benefit: Deliver high-quality communications that are on-brand, using brand-approved assets.

practices.title: Measure Performance
practices.text: Evaluate communication systems using a clear criterion. Update criteria regularly and identify best practices for future use.
practices.benefit: Deliver high-quality communications by setting benchmarks and identifying best practices.

practices.title: Improve Performance
practices.text: Identify and record opportunities for future improvement.
practices.benefit: Improve the chapter's capability to meet its goals and objectives.

focusAreas.name: Continuous Improvement
intro: Continuous improvement focuses on making small changes to enhance processes and services. It encourages chapter leaders and volunteers to think critically, share improvement ideas, and use resources to implement them.
This can involve regular strategy planning sessions to set goals and align with both local context and ISACA Global initiatives.

why.title: Chapter Relevance
why.text: Fosters a culture of learning and innovation, enabling chapters to respond to member needs, emerging trends, and technological advancements.

why.title: Seamless Experiences
why.text: Contributes to cost savings, increased productivity, and member satisfaction.

why.title: Participation Boost
why.text: Meets and exceeds member expectations in a culture where chapter leaders and volunteers participate in problem-solving, share insights, and contribute to the work.

practiceAreas.name: Performance Management
practiceAreas.whatItIs: Performance management involves continuously identifying and analyzing areas for enhancement. It aims to boost efficiency, improve quality, and deliver value while reducing waste, variation, and defects. Transparency fosters trust among chapter leadership, members, and stakeholders.

why.title: Resource Optimization
why.text: Optimizes the use of time, resources, and funding.

why.title: Success Recognition
why.text: Celebrates its achievements and those of its volunteers.

why.title: Future Improvements
why.text: Identifies and fixes gaps in achieving desired outcomes.

practices.title: Evaluate Performance
practices.text: Identify and collect measurement methods to assess performance. Record and communicate results.
practices.benefit: Boost chances of meeting objectives.

practices.title: Identify Performance Opportunities
practices.text: Review and address performance opportunities as data is collected and analyzed. Make suggestions and improvements with constraints in mind.
practices.benefit: Meet objectives and avoid rework.

practices.title: Store Measurement Data
practices.text: Store measurement data, specs, and analysis results while ensuring data quality. Follow storage procedures and make data accessible for use.
practices.benefit: Analyze performance to increase the chances of repeating success.

practices.title: Drive Implementation
practices.text: Address opportunities by implementing and managing them to completion.
practices.benefit: Meet performance objectives.

practices.title: Communicate Results
practices.text: Share performance results and document them in reports.
practices.benefit: Improve coordination and understanding of performance to reduce waste and boost the likelihood of achieving objectives.

practiceAreas.name: Resource Optimization
practiceAreas.whatItIs: Resource optimization ensures a chapter uses its resources efficiently. This involves managing volunteers, time, money, and materials effectively.

why.title: Financial Health
why.text: By using resources efficiently, chapters can reduce costs on services, materials, and other expenses.

why.title: Chapter Optimization
why.text: Chapters can accomplish more in less time by using resources effectively. Defining volunteer roles and setting clear expectations also facilitate efficient delegation and enhance contributions.Morale Boost: When members and volunteers have the necessary resources, they're happier, more productive, and more engaged.

why.title: Satisfaction Guarantee
why.text: Member satisfaction increases when chapters deliver products or services on time and within budget.

practices.title: Establish an Organizational Strategy
practices.text: Develop a strategy for chapter operations by defining roles and tasks. Keep resources current and effectively manage activities and processes. Train stakeholders on methods and tools for better efficiency.
practices.benefit: Lower the effort and cost of chapter activities while boosting efficiency.

practices.title: Evaluate Chapter Effectiveness
practices.text: Regularly review the chapter's effectiveness and act on the findings. Check outcomes, highlight best practices, and find areas to improve. Implement and share new ideas to boost resource efficiency.
practices.benefit: Increase efficient use of chapter resources.

practiceAreas.name: New Programs & Projects
practiceAreas.whatItIs: Managing new programs and projects is a complete, detailed implementation process.

why.title: Strategic Advancement
why.text: Aligns with ISACA’s and the chapter’s strategic goals and focuses on the most important things.

why.title: Budget Adherence
why.text: New programs and projects are completed on time and within budget without wasting resources.

why.title: Contextual Relevance
why.text: New programs and projects are locally relevant and meet the needs of the chapter’s stakeholders.

why.title: Risk Prevention
why.text: Careful planning and effective management help reduce risk.

why.title: Maximized Value
why.text: Thoughtfully designed programs and projects can benefit the chapter when effectively implemented.

why.title: Credibility Boost
why.text: A reputation for innovation can help chapters to attract and retain members.

practices.title: Review Chapter Strategy
practices.text: Review the chapter strategy and document new objectives for programs and projects.
practices.benefit: Align with the overall chapter strategy.

practices.title: Identify New Programs & Projects
practices.text: Identify, record, and update new programs and projects linked to the chapter.
practices.benefit: Minimize risk impacts and leverage new programs and projects to meet objectives.

practices.title: Analyze Opportunities
practices.text: Analyze new programs and projects, identifying their benefits and costs. Prioritize them based on this analysis, rank them accordingly, and compile a report.
practices.benefit: Reduce the impact of risks and leverage opportunities.

practices.title: Determine Estimates
practices.text: Develop high-level estimates for new programs and projects by reviewing needs and assumptions with stakeholders.
practices.benefit: Avoid pursuing efforts that may result in budget overruns.

practices.title: Align on Scope
practices.text: Develop and update the scope for estimates. Collaborate with stakeholders to define requirements and objectives, gathering details on size, effort, cost, resources, and duration. Identify any constraints and boundaries within the scope.
practices.benefit: Meet objectives and avoiding rework.

practices.title: Update Estimates
practices.text: Update chapter budget estimates using suitable methods to gauge its size and complexity.
practices.benefit: Enable tracking and timely corrective actions to deliver on time and within budget.

practices.title: Establish a Budget
practices.text: Develop and document the chapter budget using size estimates and historical data.
practices.benefit: Enable a better basis for commitments and improve the performance of the chapter.

practices.title: Assemble & Deliver Solutions
practices.text: Assemble and deliver the solution and document all information needed for implementation.
practices.benefit: Enable member satisfaction by assembling and delivering a usable solution.
